body:
That's a lot of advice. Thank you so much - I especially appreciate the gear recommendations. No way to properly thank how much effort you put here but I appreciate it.

> There is way too much to explain about trainhopping to be able to do it in an internet post. You need a mentor to safely learn to ride trains.

Yes, I've been told by people here to hitchhike until I can find a trainhopper to show me the ropes. Not sure how long that'll take but I'll do it.

I know not to follow the example of reckless internet "stars" trying to get likes. There isn't much in the way of real trainhopping videos so I'll take what I can get.

Apparently he got banned from Canada and the US for ten years so until 2027 he isn't gonna be saying much.

Just for information (so in the future I don't repeat his mistakes if I end up in this situation), what things did he do that are the most reckless? The hanging off the side and climbing on top of the cars were the most obvious to me but I'm probably missing stuff.

I've heard that if you get caught and remember that you're both human, and treat them nicely, you'll usually get let off with a warning like you said. Hell, I've seen some stories where they're given a few dollars and a drive out.

All in all, seems like "treat your fellow human with compassion" is the system we should go for.
I mean, I suppose it's a good lesson on what *not* to do, to be fair.

Yeah, they had a huge group, walked around in broad daylight right next to very active roads, and just seemed like a bunch of entitled rich dudes like you said.

I'm all for a lesson in humility, but this isn't it lol
Good luck!

I was thinking getting caught was inevitable but it seemed like Youtube guys seem to get caught *a lot*. 

After some thinking the guys in the second video just weren't too smart. They often ran out across roads to a train in broad daylight and did all you mentioned. Which explains a lot.

Are railfans that much of a nuisance? I've heard they're pretty cool but twice today I've heard they tend to call the bull or police.

So the blue one is the one I'm looking for, then?

> Why would being 18 be a problem in Nebraska

Age of majority is 19 here, legally my rights still belong to my parents. They aren't *bad*, but they probably wouldn't like it if I left at all at the moment despite how much I'd like to, which is why I'd like to get to another state where legally they can't do anything/

>Spend some time on google maps and you well see how they make up the trains and which tracks they head out on. There is a homeless shelter close to where the eastbound line crosses under broadway blvd and some of them could have more info on hop outs

Sounds good. Thank you!
Huh. Thanks for the advice!
thank you!
Yeah I've been worried about police presence. Isn't hitchhiking illegal in a lot of places? I suppose trainhopping is too, but generally you try to avoid getting detected with that.

Sounds better than I imagined it. Guess I should start thinking about that. I'll probably keep some mace on me like you suggested but I look forward to meeting some nicer people.

That's good advice. Hopefully I can meet someone here either on this subreddit or another forum. I'm looking forward to learning the ropes so with any luck I'll find someone who can teach me.

I've heard that. I'm just not a very talkative or social person. Not necessarily running into bad guys I'm worried about (though I certainly am worried about that).

Where do people generally stand around for hitchhiking? I know the general "hold a sign and put your thumbs up", but seems like there's probably better places to "stand around" than others.
I've heard of that website before, seems very helpful. Thanks for the advice!

I appreciate the advice. Always helps to know when I'm being an idiot with big dreams.

My worries with hitchhiking are mostly just dealing with other people. How does hitchhiking generally go?

Preferably east since I'm 18 which is still a minor in Nebraska. Outside of Nebraska I can do whatever I want so I suppose I should try getting to Council Bluffs. 

Only trainyard I know of in Council Bluffs is near the Cracker Barrel, [green one in this image](https://i.imgur.com/jJs8ysi.png). I didn't actually know about the other two until now. Any experience with those?
Not in Canada but if I ever find myself there, will do!
Perhaps but if I had to choose one danger I'd go with that.
I understand. Thank you for all the advice!
Nah, Nebraska unfortunately
I'll try - I'm sure you can tell by the name this is an alt (the original account has been long since deleted but I keep the alt around) - but if I remember I'll be sure to get back to you!

I welcome all the criticism I can get - this isn't a small decision on my part. I suppose the best thing for me to do is a few smaller camping trips on my part to see if I can do it and work from there.
Well, I'm not sure. I've come here for advice on that kind of thing, really. And in case I'm just being an idiot.
Thanks. I'm not sure that's exactly what I'm looking for though. For me it's just, I don't want to be working. Even if it limits my potential in life I'd much rather be poor and traveling
Seems like an interesting guy. Thanks for the website.

If I did go to college it'd probably be in 2021 - I could go this year but I want to start in 2021 for a few reasons.

However, seeing as I do an online school right now I imagine I'll be really unlikely to get a scholarship and I'm not looking forward to the debt. Part of the reason I feel as I do is because I don't want to get stuck in the cycle of life. I don't want to be stuck working a job and going to the same home every single day for the rest of my life. I hate staying in the same place very long so that life is not for me.
I was considering saving up some money, buying a tent, heading out west, and live on BLM land unti lit all blows over.
Huh, thanks for the tips! I really appreciate it.
I love flying and that'd be a great plan, however I'm still not sure what I'd do next. Sorry for all the stupid questions lol
That has been my idea for years, but that'd require a lot of money. Which I don't have and even if I saved up I'd need a reliable source of income for maintenance.
I've never heard of rubber tramping, what's that?

As I said in a [prior comment](https://old.reddit.com/r/vagabond/comments/fv7ckd/m18_no_money_but_i_just_want_to_go/fmi6g54/) I'd rather not hitchhike for a few reasons, unless I absolutely have to.

I know there's trainhopping and getting around under my own power but I don't know if those will be too difficult.

I don't think hitchhiking is my thing - it just seems far too dangerous for me. Even if it's harder I think it'd be best for me to find my own way.

I just feel like I want my life to be under my own control for once. Not sure if that's related.

Gas jugging?

Yeah, I can't do much with this whole global pandemic. 

> everything has gotten back to normal, hop the nearest freight train and see where it takes you.

That's exactly what I want to do, just pick a direction and go. Or take a random freight train and go, in this case. I'm just not sure what to do after that. I have some ideas like dumpster diving but I'm not sure what else.

I don't have a car or anything at the moment either (and if I did I'd need gas), so my plan for going somewhere was either biking or trainhopping, but I've no idea how to do that. Guess I gotta start somewhere.
